items.question: What great attainment makes one dear to the yoginīs?
premises: Enjoyment and liberation together form a great accomplishment
Such accomplishment relates to the yoginīs
Possessing it makes one dear to them
items.inference: One who attains the great accomplishment of enjoyment and liberation becomes dear to the yoginīs
items.plain_english: He may become dear to the yoginīs through the great accomplishment of both enjoyment and liberation.

items.question: Which chapter concludes upon emergence in the moon island?
premises: A chapter is identified as ninth
Its conclusion is marked by emergence
The emergence occurs in the moon island
items.inference: The ninth chapter concludes with emergence in the moon island
items.plain_english: The ninth chapter, emerged in the moon island, is concluded.

items.question: How should the practitioner visualize the self amid surrounding fire?
premises: The self is visualized as surrounded by fire
The self is positioned in a specific posture
The posture involves standing on one foot
items.inference: The practitioner should visualize the self surrounded by fire and standing on one foot
items.plain_english: One should visualize the self surrounded by fire, standing on one foot.

items.question: What request is made to the god regarding the determination of knowledge?
premises: The speaker addresses the god directly
The speaker asks for a determination of knowledge
The speaker requests it be made manifest now
items.inference: The speaker asks the god to make the determination of knowledge manifest today
items.plain_english: O God, make the determination of knowledge manifest to me today.

items.question: What division does the seeker wish to know fully without end?
premises: A division is specified as eight octads
The seeker desires full knowledge of it
The desire for knowledge is expressed as endless
items.inference: The seeker wishes to know fully and endlessly the division of the eight octads
items.plain_english: And to know fully and endlessly the division of the eight octads.

items.question: How is the wheel in the secret place quickly accomplished, O Bhairava?
premises: A wheel is located in a secret place
The speaker asks about its accomplishment
The accomplishment is described as quick
items.inference: The question seeks to know how the wheel in the secret place is quickly accomplished
items.plain_english: O Bhairava, how is the wheel in the secret place quickly accomplished?

items.question: What rare matter has the great goddess asked of the speaker?
premises: The speaker expresses strong approval
The great goddess has asked a question
What is asked is hard to obtain even for gods
items.inference: The great goddess has asked about something rare and hard for the gods to obtain
items.plain_english: Well said, well said, O great goddess; you have asked me about something hard for even the gods to obtain.

items.question: Which syllables correspond to the brahmarandhra and the forehead locations?
premises: The syllable kṣa is associated with the brahmarandhra state
The syllable laṃ is associated with another location
That location is the forehead
items.inference: The syllable kṣa corresponds to the brahmarandhra and the syllable laṃ to the forehead
uncertainties: lalāṭayoḥ is dual in form though often used for the forehead region
items.plain_english: The syllable kṣa is the state of the brahmarandhra, and the syllable laṃ is in the forehead.

items.question: Which syllables are assigned to the throat region and the heart?
premises: The syllable ṣa is placed in the throat region
The syllable śa is placed in another location
That location is the heart
items.inference: The syllable ṣa corresponds to the throat region and the syllable śa to the heart
items.plain_english: The syllable ṣa is in the throat region, and the syllable śa is then in the heart.

items.question: What instruction follows the declaration of the place-wheels to the beloved?
premises: The place-wheels have been declared
Their meditation is to be taught
The beloved is commanded to listen
items.inference: After declaring the place-wheels, the speaker instructs the beloved to hear their meditation
items.plain_english: Thus the place-wheels have been declared; now hear their meditation, O beloved.

items.question: How is the divine lotus of the first octad described in form?
premises: A divine lotus is the object of description
It has eight spokes or petals
It is adorned by the first octad
items.inference: The divine lotus is eight-spoked and adorned by the first octad
items.plain_english: A divine eight-spoked lotus, adorned by the first octad.

rows.grounds: object to abandon; sandhi before ca

items.question: What conduct should a practitioner with balanced mind abandon through practice?
premises: Practice leads to a balanced mind
A certain conduct is to be given up
That conduct is village dharma
items.inference: Through practice, one with a balanced mind should abandon village dharma
uncertainties: grāma-dharmañ may refer to conventional worldly duties
items.plain_english: Through practice, with an even mind, one should abandon the dharma of the village.

items.question: What powers arise from this practice, including distant hearing and binding paralysis?
premises: Knowledge of distant hearing is attained
Paralysis of bonds is attained
These are presented as results to the beloved
items.inference: The practice yields knowledge of distant hearing and the power to paralyze bonds
uncertainties: pāśa-stobham could mean arresting or stopping bonds
items.plain_english: Knowledge of hearing from afar, and likewise the paralysis of bonds, O beloved.

items.question: What further attainments, stated briefly, include immortality and transformation?
premises: Immortality is named as an attainment
Transformation is named as another attainment
These are stated in brief to the goddess
items.inference: In brief, the attainments include immortality and transformation
items.plain_english: Likewise immortality and, in brief, transformation, O goddess.

items.question: How is the second eight-petaled center characterized by fiery meditation?
premises: A second center is described
It has eight petals
It is well illuminated by meditation on fire
items.inference: The second eight-petaled center is well illuminated through meditation on fire
items.plain_english: The second is eight-petaled, well illuminated by meditation on fire.

items.question: What ability arises for one whose mind is absorbed in single-pointed meditation?
premises: The mind becomes absorbed in one-pointed meditation
An action of making forms occurs
The forms are produced in many ways
items.inference: One whose mind is absorbed in single-pointed meditation can assume many forms
items.plain_english: One whose mind is absorbed in single-pointed meditation can assume many forms.

items.question: What destructive power manifests when the practitioner becomes angry?
premises: Anger is the triggering condition
The power to destroy is activated
The entire triple world with moving and unmoving beings is affected
items.inference: When angry, the practitioner can destroy the entire triple world with all moving and unmoving beings
items.plain_english: When angry, he can destroy the entire triple world, with all that moves and does not move.

items.question: What liberating function is attributed to the third great wheel?
premises: A third great wheel is identified
It has a liberating function
Its liberation pertains to the nine principles
items.inference: The third great wheel is the liberator from the nine principles
items.plain_english: The third is the great wheel, the liberator from the nine principles.

items.question: What bodily and perceptual attainments result from this wheel's practice?
premises: Destruction of wrinkles and grey hair is attained
Another attainment concerns perception
That perception extends to seeing from very far away
items.inference: The practice brings destruction of wrinkles and grey hair and the ability to see from very far away
items.plain_english: It brings the destruction of wrinkles and grey hair, and likewise the ability to see from very far away.

rows.grounds: object of intent; sandhi before ca

items.question: What practice should one perform in solitude while intent on meditation?
premises: The practice is to be done in solitude
The practitioner should be intent on meditation
The practitioner is instructed to create many forms
items.inference: In solitude, intent on meditation, one should create many forms
items.plain_english: In solitude, intent on meditation, create many forms.

items.question: What result does constant dedicated practice produce for the practitioner?
premises: The practitioner is intent on constant practice
A specific result is produced
That result is immortality
items.inference: One intent on constant practice attains immortality
items.plain_english: Indeed, one intent on constant practice attains immortality.

items.question: How does abstaining from food by day affect death from aging?
premises: Non-eating by day is practiced
Death associated with age is confronted
The practitioner will overcome or pass beyond it
items.inference: By abstaining from food during the day, one will overcome death from aging
uncertainties: gamiṣyate with mṛtyuṃ may imply going beyond or reaching death; context suggests overcoming
items.plain_english: By abstaining from food during the day, one will overcome death from aging.

items.question: What bodily form results from constant yogic practice over sixteen years?
premises: Constant practice is performed through yoga
The duration is two times eight years
A specific bodily form results
items.inference: Through constant yogic practice, one attains the form of a sixteen-year-old
items.plain_english: Through constant yogic practice, one attains the form of a sixteen-year-old.

items.question: What contemplative visualization enables one to shake the triple world?
premises: A smoke-colored visualization is prescribed
The contemplation is to be done always
This contemplation results in shaking the triple world
items.inference: By always contemplating a smoke-colored form, one can shake the triple world
items.plain_english: Always contemplating a smoke-colored form, one can shake the triple world, O beloved.
